# Pilot — UK elections (Democracy Club)

**Real data.** Generated by `tools/adapters/elections-democracyclub.py` from the Democracy
Club API, which publishes every UK election — some 42,000 ballots — with voting systems,
seats contested, candidacies, parties and declared results.

```bash
python3 tools/adapters/elections-democracyclub.py --date 2024-05-02 --limit 40 \
  --out examples/pilot-uk-elections
```

2 May 2024: 5 elections, 40 contests, 292 candidates, 18 parties. 397 entities.

The UK runs several electoral systems side by side, which makes it the right test of the
profile's claim that `electoralSystem` is what lets election data travel.

## The profile held

Real results validated first time, with no schema change. `AMS` — the Additional Member
System used for the London Assembly — maps to `mmp`, and first-past-the-post contests sit
alongside it in the same election. Candidacies, parties, elected flags and vote counts all
mapped directly.

## A design decision I nearly reversed for the wrong reason

The profile deliberately does **not** store turnout, on the grounds that a percentage should
be recomputable from the register — so `registeredVoters` and `ballotsCast` are stored and
turnout is derived.

Reading the first sample I concluded Democracy Club publishes `turnout_percentage` without an
electorate, which would have made the headline number of an election unrepresentable. I added
a `reportedTurnoutPercentage` field to carry it.

**That was wrong.** `total_electorate` is published; I had misread my own probe output. The
field was reverted and the adapter now reads the electorate properly. The original design was
right, and it is visibly better:

```
Barnet and Camden     163,655 / 413,809 = 39.5%     (Democracy Club publishes 40.0%)
Bexley and Bromley    203,904 / 421,800 = 48.3%
```

Democracy Club rounds turnout to one decimal place. Storing the register recovers the real
figure; storing the percentage would have locked in the rounding. That is exactly the argument
the profile made, now demonstrated rather than asserted.

`registeredVoters` was added to `Contest` as well as `Election`, because the register is drawn
per constituency and turnout is only meaningful against the electorate that could vote in that
race.

## A latent bug in the shapes

Six SHACL shapes listed the jurisdiction class as `AdministrativeArea` or `City` only, omitting
`Country` and `State` — which the `_core` jurisdiction schema has permitted since it was
written. It surfaced here because this is the first election pilot with a national
jurisdiction, but it would have failed for any national-level publisher using
`Post.representsJurisdiction`, `ServiceRequest.jurisdiction`, `AlertArea.jurisdiction`,
`Permit.validIn` or `Contest.representsJurisdiction`.

Normalised to the full set across all six.

## What is genuinely missing

**17 of 40 contests publish no electorate.** Local election returns often carry turnout as a
percentage with no register behind it. The profile declines to store the derived figure, so
that turnout is simply absent for those contests rather than recorded at a precision that
cannot be recomputed. That is the intended behaviour, and it is a real limit worth stating:
**the profile prefers a gap to a number it cannot vouch for.**

**One contest's reported turnout differs from valid plus spoilt ballots.** Reported by the
adapter rather than reconciled, since the discrepancy belongs to the returning officer's
declaration.
